result.title: Beyond Aggregate Accuracy: Item-Level Transitions in Prompt Optimization
result.summary: Automatic prompt optimization (APO) uses feedback from model responses to improve prompts automatically. However, its effectiveness is usually measured through overall scores, which do not reveal which questions become correct, which previously correct answers become wrong, or whether improvements extend to unseen questions. We introduce Reflective Feedback-Driven Prompt Optimization (RFDPO), a tool that tracks recoveries (incorrect to correct), regressions (correct to incorrect), and churn (all changed outcomes). RFDPO uses this feedback to guide subsequent revisions and records prompt changes throughout optimization. We evaluate RFDPO across five benchmarks covering law, knowledge, instruction following, mathematics, and privacy, using GPT-5 as the optimizer and GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1 Mini as solvers. Our results show that overall accuracy can hide substantial changes: in five of nine configurations, churn was at least five times the absolute net change, and a single-item net change concealed up to 17 changed outcomes. Average validation gains were 7.9 percentage points, compared with 5.2 points on held-out tests. In a controlled ablation on LegalBench-Hearsay, item-level feedback reduced churn by 40% ($p=0.024$) while maintaining similar net gains. These findings motivate reporting recovery, regression, churn, and performance on unseen data alongside overall accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RFDPO，在自动 prompt 优化中用「恢复／退化／总变动」等逐题结果转移指标替代聚合准确率，并在法律、知识、指令遵循、数学与隐私五个基准上比较验证集与留出测试的增益。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文属于 prompt 优化的评价方法学，与 LVR 无直接关系；但其「逐样本转移＋churn」视角可能为 LVR 评价提供线索，用于核查 latent 训练或 THINK/LOOK/STOP 策略是否在提高整体表现的同时掩盖大量逐题得失，以及收益是否泛化到未见问题。
